sentences.text: Enterocloster aldenensis is described as an organism typically found in the gut that occasionally acts as an opportunistic pathogen; one strain came from a scrotal tissue sample in Southern Thailand.

That strain was first misidentified as Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron by mass spectrometry, was reclassified after whole-genome sequencing, and shared antimicrobial resistance genes including poxtA, vanYG, vanWI and vanTG.
A study of tryptophan metabolism identified Enterocloster aldenensis as a producer of indole-3-propionate from indole-3-lactate but not from tryptophan, in cross-feeding with Lachnospira eligens.
